scope: Credential/runtime service and explicit-consent handler, not yet registered as a production route or UI action.
implemented: Auth service deletion requires the existing durable per-account attempt limiter, active logical sign-in, current password and enabled second factor. Missing security infrastructure fails closed.

The verified password hash and MFA enabled-secret state are matched again inside the anonymization transaction. A concurrent factor enrollment/change after proof rejects the transition rather than applying a stale security decision.

Successful durable anonymization invokes the existing user-cache invalidation, all-user WebSocket disconnect and voice-disconnect collaborators. Failed transition does not revoke the caller or report success.

Handler requires account affinity, active human session, bounded single JSON object, no unknown fields, password, separate confirmation flag and exact DELETE text. Ownership/application/admin blockers have distinct recoverable error codes.

No Set-Cookie is emitted, so a late account-bound response cannot clear a newer shared-cookie login. Success explicitly reports shared history retained and personal-asset cleanup queued, not all blobs already removed.
Handler and AuthOption exist but no deletion route, production repository option or UI action has been wired yet; operational cleanup scheduling and full consent UX must land before exposure.
